nice_title: Stable angina: management / Acute coronary syndromes

first_line_treatment.indication: All patients with IHD regardless of cholesterol level
All IHD patients, especially with LV dysfunction, diabetes, or hypertension

second_line_anti_anginal.drug_class: Calcium channel blocker (if beta-blocker insufficient or intolerant)
examples: Verapamil (if no HF, not with BB)
second_line_anti_anginal.indication: Add to or replace beta-blocker for angina

second_line_anti_anginal.notes: Nitrate-free interval needed to prevent tolerance

acute_management.GTN: Sublingual GTN spray for acute angina episodes
acute_management.dual_antiplatelet: Aspirin + Ticagrelor or Clopidogrel after ACS for 12 months
acute_management.anticoagulation: Fondaparinux or Enoxaparin during ACS admission

contraindicated_drugs.reason: Risk of heart block and asystole

monitoring: Lipid profile: 3 months after starting statin, then annually
BP: at every review (target <140/90, <130/80 if diabetes)
Renal function: annually if on ACE-I
Consider stress test or angiography if symptoms worsen
non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation (most important modifiable risk factor)
Regular exercise: 150 min/week (cardiac rehabilitation after events)
referral_criteria: Consider revascularisation (PCI or CABG) if medical therapy insufficient
